heuristics.name: Derive legal-effect type
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Assign legal_effect_type for a retained proposition using deterministic precedence: explicit priority cues, boilerplate, definition structure, substantive textual modals, extracted provision_type (non-cross-reference), cross-reference-only cues, then deferred provision_type cross_reference, else unknown.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a E2 (path 2-a-ii): priority cue 'shall not apply' wins as explicit_exception_cue → derogation, even when the model proposed provision_type=exception.

heuristics.name: Attach applicable exception context
heuristics.plain_english_summary: When an exception_to relationship targets a LegalRuleGroup (or proposition), the effective-law composer attaches the exception proposition as applicable_exception on each expanded target member. This is a presentation/context projection of the existing typed relationship, not a new inferred edge.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a: E1/E2/E3 become applicable_exception on P1 and P2 via the paragraph-1 group.

heuristics.name: Attach exception-target context
heuristics.plain_english_summary: For each exception_to expansion, attach the displaced rule propositions as exception_target on the exception proposition. Members come from the targeted group (or the direct proposition target). This projects the existing exception_to relationship into reviewer-facing context; it is not a separate inferred relationship.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a: P1 and P2 appear as exception_target on E1, E2, and E3.

heuristics.name: Attach trigger-condition context
heuristics.plain_english_summary: When a triggered_by relationship targets a LegalRuleGroup (or proposition), attach each expanded target member as trigger_condition on the relationship source only. Current semantics are source-only: no reverse trigger context is projected onto the trigger propositions.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a: E1/E2/E3 become trigger_condition on P3; P3 is not projected backwards onto E1/E2/E3.

heuristics.name: Prefer typed context over generic locator
heuristics.plain_english_summary: When a generic locator required-context entry resolves only to propositions already represented by typed legal-relationship context on the same statement, omit that generic duplicate. Typed context has priority only where the generic entry represents the same source/target legal connection. Unrelated ordinary references (for example Article 14 beside a paragraph-1 exception) remain.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a E3: paragraph-1 generic locator suppressed; Article 14 ordinary referenced_locator retained.

heuristics.name: Create shared-fragment LegalRuleGroup
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Law Proposition Extractor groups two or more retained propositions that share the same source_record_id, source_snapshot_id, and source_fragment_id when that fragment has a reliable canonical locator. Grouping is structural (shared source fragment), not textual similarity, shared topic, shared legal-effect classification, or model judgment. Members are ordered by deterministic source order. Single-member fragments, unreliable locators, mixed source/snapshot/fragment buckets, article-level aggregates, and descendant roll-ups do not form groups.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a paragraph 1 yields one group for P1+P2; paragraph 3 alone does not form a group.

heuristics.name: Infer exception_to relationship
heuristics.plain_english_summary: When a derogation/exception proposition contains a supported exception cue, bind the reference inside that cue span and infer an exception_to relationship to the safely resolved target. References outside the cue-target association remain ordinary contextual references.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a E3: 'Paragraph 1 shall not apply' → exception_to article:49a:paragraph:1; Article 14 stays ordinary.

heuristics.name: Infer triggered_by relationship
heuristics.plain_english_summary: When a proposition contains supported trigger phrasing such as 'in the cases referred to in …', bind the cue-span reference and infer a triggered_by relationship to the safely resolved target.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a P3: 'in the cases referred to in Article 49a(2)' → triggered_by article:49a:paragraph:2.

heuristics.name: Prefer LegalRuleGroup as relationship target
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Where the resolved provision has one persisted LegalRuleGroup in the same source/snapshot scope, Law Proposition Extractor targets the group so downstream context can be inherited by all of its member propositions. Falls back to a unique retained proposition; never fans out to multiple targets.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a exception_to targets the paragraph-1 group (P1+P2), not either paragraph-1 proposition individually.

heuristics.name: Prefer required ancestor over focus descendant
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Suppress a focus-selected descendant when an explicitly required selected ancestor already covers its operative text and structured-list terminals.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a paragraph 2(a) is not separately extracted because required paragraph 2 covers its structured-list terminals.

heuristics.name: Prefer selected structural children
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Suppress extraction of a selected parent when every substantive direct child is selected and those children collectively cover the parent's operative text.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a is not extracted because paragraphs 1–3 cover its operative text.

heuristics.name: Required locator selection
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Select a fragment for extraction when its locator is listed in the run's required locators configuration.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a paragraph 1 is selected because the case requires article:49a:paragraph:1.

heuristics.name: Compose structured-list terminal leaf
heuristics.plain_english_summary: Compose the operative rule represented by a terminal structured-list path by combining the governing stem, any intermediate branch context, and the terminal leaf; attach canonical structured-list metadata and retain the composed candidate as a proposition.
heuristics.example_summary: Article 49a path 2-a-ii is retained by combining the paragraph-2 stem, branch (a), and terminal point (ii).
